category_title: Middle school students who disengage and use ritualistic rule-following when encountering fractions
scenario_title: Solving arithmetic exercises and algebraic equations
minimal_context: The student is sitting one-on-one with an interviewer and working on paper to solve the arithmetic exercise 2/3 * 9.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please solve this arithmetic exercise on the paper: 2/3 * 9.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks at paper) Now, here I'll put two thirds times nine and I'll make from it one thing so it will be easier for me... So, here I'll write... I'll do like this, two times nine divided by three times one. (Looks at interviewer) Is it right to do like that?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What do you think you should do next?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Quietly, biting lip, looking down) With fractions I'm not good so I don't know... (Looks up at interviewer, raised, contracted eyebrows, slightly anxious expression) Maybe by half?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just keep trying to solve it.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Thinks) It can be simplified. (Erases what she has written) Because I have to solve the exercise from the beginning... I simplify the nine and then I'll get three and one.

task.content: Solving the arithmetic exercise '2/3 * 9' and looking for a substitution set

context.time_context: First mathematical interview and final 7th-grade interview

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When unsure of a step while solving an exercise
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Erases what she has written because 'I have to solve the exercise from the beginning', looks at interviewer asking 'Is it right to do like that?'
related_quotes: Is it right to do like that?

behavior_patterns.condition: When provided with heavy scaffolding and leading questions
